elements.element: The liability cap applies mutually to both Parties.
elements.evidence: Section 15.3(b) limits “the total liability of either Party.”

elements.element: The mutual cap equals the greater of (a) fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The clause caps liability at amounts paid or payable during the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim, but contains no USD 1,000,000 floor or greater-of mechanism and uses a different lookback trigger.
The mutual exclusion lists lost profits, consequential, punitive and incidental damages, but does not expressly exclude indirect damages.
Section 15.3(a) provides that neither Party is liable to the other for consequential damages.

elements.element: Liability for breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Breach of a Party’s confidentiality obligations is an Excluded Claim expressly not subject to the cap.

elements.element: Liability for breach of data protection obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No carve-out addresses data protection obligations.

elements.element: Liability for breach of security obligations is uncapped.

elements.evidence: A Party’s indemnification obligations under Section 15.1 are Excluded Claims expressly not subject to the cap.

elements.element: Liability for wilful misconduct is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Wilful misconduct is an Excluded Claim expressly not subject to the cap.

result.reason: The operative language reaches the fallback: it establishes a mutual 12-month cap and uncaps indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. It does not reach the preferred position because it omits the USD 1,000,000 greater-of floor, data protection and security carve-outs, an express indirect-damages exclusion, and the treatment of Customer payment obligations. It is not minimal relative to the completed fallback because it also adds fraud and IP-infringement carve-outs while still failing to complete the preferred position. The drafting is generally coherent but uses “amounts” rather than fees, changes the preferred lookback from the claim to the event giving rise to it, limits the indemnity carve-out specifically to Section 15.1, and retains a stray duplicated period.
